limits.text: 01Helix is nonclinical: not a diagnostic, variant classification or medical advice tool. ClinVar's classification is shown as a database record with its review status, not as advice.

02The curated sets of this build are BRCA1, CFTR, FAAH2, HBB and SLC6A3; other genes are refused rather than built from uncurated data. This set (SLC6A3) carries the gene, its MANE Select transcript and sequences, the protein record and its curated variant, one experimental structure (PDB 8Y2C) and a predicted model (listed, not loaded).

03The data are a snapshot of public records with a retrieval date and record versions (see Evidence World), not a live feed. Records change between builds. ClinVar's record for R85W is VCV000421417.2 in this build.

048Y2C (electron microscopy) is a structure of the reference protein: the 3D view shows the reference residue Arg 85; the variant residue of R85W is not modelled in 3D, and the change is compared on the sequence only.

05The contacts shown for Arg 85 are computed in the deposited asymmetric unit, within the residue's own chain (asymmetric unit, model 1, no symmetry mates; the residue's own chain included beyond its covalent neighbours (one mapped chain)). Symmetry-related molecules were not generated, so contacts across them are not assessed.
06One numbering applies to Q01959: translated (HGVS, UniProt; Met = 1), which the residue numbers of 8Y2C follow. Helix still maps through the SIFTS record, never by assuming the two are equal.

07Codon k maps to protein position k because the CDS translates exactly to UniProt Q01959. SIFTS maps positions 66 to 620 onto 8Y2C chain A; positions outside the deposited coordinates and the stop codon have no structure residue.

088Y2C covers residues 66 to 620 of 620 (529 observed positions, 85.3 %; ELECTRON MICROSCOPY, 3.16 A). The entry covers 529 of the protein's 620 residues; the rest has no experimental coordinates in this set, and a predicted model never stands in for it.
09The DNA helix is illustrative geometry: the bases, their order and the exons are real, the shape and spacing are not to scale.
10The AlphaFold model of Q01959 is listed as a computational prediction but is never used to place the variant and is not loaded.

11A language model, when one is available, only proposes a plan of fixed actions; deterministic code checks every identifier and executes. Its wording is never a scientific claim. Its suggested next questions are shown only when a fixed filter finds them nonclinical and answerable with the curated data. Without a model, a rule-based planner answers a limited set of questions.
12Evidence World v1 is a page layer, not yet a world the planner can enter: the plan vocabulary has no evidence world, and adding one would change the Phase 3 prompt.

13Pathway World v1 shows Reactome membership only: which curated pathways list the protein (a database annotation, class 2) and the participants of the opened one as named entities. It draws no arrows, no reactions and no mechanism, and says nothing about the effect of any variant on a pathway; the pathway it opens on is the rule's choice (fewest participants among non-disease pathways with a diagram), not a statement of importance.

14The disease associations in Evidence World are Open Targets database annotations (class 2): each score aggregates the platform's evidence for a target-disease pair, with the scores of share-alike or restricted sources dropped. An association, never causal; a score aggregates evidence, it does not state that the gene causes the disease; nothing here is a diagnosis, and no world or answer is built on an association.
15Tested in headless Chrome on one Mac. Safari, Firefox and the desktop webview were not run in this phase.
